timing_note: exit codes and every number below are deterministic; wall-clock timings are magnitude-only and deliberately not recorded here (single-run timings drift)
teaching_point: the two wait states (wait-fin / closing) are structurally identical but their completion events differ (rcv FIN vs rcv ACK of FIN). The SAME candidate group passes under the relabel reading (actions may be renamed along with states, judge generalized) and is refused under the fixed reading (event names pinned, TV 1.0 on the completion edges): which verdict is correct depends on what your actions ARE, so the model author must declare it (docs/judge-semantics.md). The padding-state swap is the fixed positive control: padding rows reference no event, so it is a genuine symmetry under both readings

first_bad.reason: 转移分布在 π 映射下的 TV 超过容忍（判据 max TV=0 零容忍）

discover_refused.why: discover's candidate search is built on the bit-string action convention (action a = flip bit a, n_actions <= n_bits); this model has 4 events on 3 bits, so discover refuses at the entry gate (InputError, exit 3) instead of crashing. Event-class models are judged by deriving candidates by hand and running check with a semantics declaration -- exactly what this rung does

two_readings.reward_layer: passes the swap under both readings (0 bad of 1 pair): reward profiles are compared as sorted per-action multisets, so the reward layer alone cannot see an event renaming -- only the transition layer under the fixed reading can
